input.command:
cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-mulaydm10-ehl-urich/84f800db-a791-4541-9835-04ece5e57fca/scratchpad/doc15.md <<'MDEOF'
# 15 — the external source: OpenStreetMap

`analysis/13_osm_layer.py`. Raw Overpass JSON over `requests`, snapped with
`scipy.spatial.cKDTree`. **No new dependencies** — osmnx and geopandas drag in
GDAL and were not worth the risk this close to a freeze.

53 tiles, 29 MB, cached under `flowstate/data/osm/` (gitignored). Fetch took
~15 min against rate-limited public mirrors; the join and report take seconds.
Once cached the demo needs no network.

## Why we needed it

We have claimed from slide one that FLOWSTATE never scores speed and only
recommends roads within the posted limit. **We had no way to check that.** The
telemetry knows how fast the crowd rode; it does not know what the sign said.
That was a hole in our own argument and a judge was entitled to walk into it.

## What it found, and it is not cosmetic

On the cells where a posted limit is known:

```
posted limit known                       39% of cells
crowd p85 above the limit by >10%        1,172 of 2,237  =  52%
median crowd p85 as a share of the limit             1.11x
```

**On half the roads where we know the limit, the crowd habitually exceeds it.**
So a little over half our demand numbers were, in part, describing what people
do when they speed.

## The fix: re-price the road, do not refuse it

Refusing those cells would be crude — a road can be excellent at 80. Instead
`apply_legal_speed` recomputes the demand at the **posted** speed. Since
`tan(theta)` goes as `v^2` at fixed radius:

```
tan(theta_legal) = tan(theta_crowd) * (v_limit / v_p85)^2
```

Effect on the 1,172 re-priced cells: **mean demand falls 9.67 -> 5.60 deg
(-4.07 deg).** The road still competes; it just competes on what it legally
offers. A cell with no posted limit (German autobahn, `maxspeed=none`) parses
to NaN and is left alone — its road class carries the meaning instead.

This is the honest version of "we never recommend speeding": not a promise on
a slide, a term in the cost function.

## BMW's RED and GREEN flags stop being inferences

Until now these were guessed from telemetry, which cannot see them — a
motorway and a fast country road look alike in a lean channel, and gravel and
tarmac look identical. Now they are tags (18-char grid, 26,987 cells):

```
RED   motorway / trunk              876 cells   3.2%   flow x0.45
RED   residential / living street 1,319 cells   4.9%   flow x0.45
RED   unpaved or cobbled              82 cells   0.3%   flow x0.55
GREEN country road, paved        14,710 cells  54.5%
```

Match quality: 17,034 of 26,987 cells (63%) found a road within 80 m, median
snap **6 m**. The unmatched third gets no flags and no penalty — absence of a
tag is never treated as evidence.

## What it did to the router

```
                     before OSM        after OSM
rider skill           12.63 deg        11.40 deg
safety gate           23.01 deg        22.59 deg
gate / hardest ridden  0.992x           1.063x
Cruise  mean demand    8.01 deg         7.02 deg
Send it mean demand   11.02 deg         9.71 deg
dial effect          +3.01 deg        +2.69 deg
```

Everything moved down, which is what re-pricing at the legal speed should do.
The gate-vs-hardest-road agreement loosened from 0.992x to 1.063x — still
within 6%, and still not something the construction forces.

## Temperature — tested, and it did NOT replicate

`sensorsoutsidetemperature` is present on 100% of corners, spanning 8.5 to
33 deg C, so the obvious idea was to derate grip on cold tarmac. We tested
whether these riders actually lean less when it is cold:

```
spearman(lean_deg, temp_c)                     -0.016   (n = 5,253)
spearman(lean/demand ratio, temp_c)            +0.040
per-trip, median lean/demand vs temp           +0.224   p = 0.24  (n = 29)
median use-ratio, <=12 C vs >24 C        0.772 vs 0.801
```

**The direction is right and the magnitude is undetectable at this sample
size.** So `mu_for_temp` ships as an explicitly labelled engineering
assumption from tyre behaviour, it feeds the **safety readout only** — grip
headroom — and it never touches the fun score. Do not claim our data
validates it. Say: "physics says cold tarmac has less grip; our 29 trips
cannot resolve it either way, so we show it as a caution, not a score."

## NDA

Nothing about BMW's data was transmitted. The query box is **rounded outward**
to generic southern Bavaria (47.3-48.1 N, 10.6-12.0 E) rather than our
measured coverage box, so not even the boundary we asked about is derived from
BMW rides. Responses are cached to disk; the demo makes no network call.

## Reproducing

```bash
cd ~/ehl_urich/flowstate
V=/Users/mulaydm10/ehl_urich/.venv/bin/python
$V analysis/13_osm_layer.py          # cached; --refetch to ignore the cache
$V app/router.py                     # now reports the OSM block

**Step 1 done — pushed as `4582af0`, both machines synced.**

## What landed

The OSM layer is fetched, cached (53 tiles, 29 MB, offline-ready) and **wired into the router's scoring** — not just sitting in a parquet file.

**The headline finding, and it isn't cosmetic:**

```
posted limit known for            39% of cells
crowd p85 above it by >10%        1,172 of 2,237 = 52%
median crowd p85 vs the limit     1.11×
```

**On half the roads where we know the limit, the crowd habitually exceeds it.** So a little over half our demand numbers were partly describing what people do *when they speed*. We'd been selling thrill that a law-abiding rider couldn't actually have.

**The fix re-prices the road instead of refusing it.** Demand is recomputed at the posted speed — since `tan θ ∝ v²` at fixed radius, `tan(θ_legal) = tan(θ_crowd) · (v_limit/v_p85)²`. Mean demand on those cells falls **9.67° → 5.60°**. A road can be excellent at 80; it just has to compete on what it *legally* offers.

That turns "we never recommend speeding" from a promise on a slide into a term in the cost function. I think that's the strongest ethics answer we have.

**BMW's flags stop being guesses.** A motorway and a fast country road look alike in a lean channel; gravel and tarmac look identical. Now they're tags:

| | cells | effect |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 motorway/trunk | 876 (3.2%) | flow ×0.45 |
| 🔴 residential/living street | 1,319 (4.9%) | flow ×0.45 |
| 🔴 unpaved/cobbled | 82 (0.3%) | flow ×0.55 |
| 🟢 country road, paved | 14,710 (54.5%) | — |

63% of cells matched a road within 80 m, median snap **6 m**. The unmatched third gets no flags — absence of a tag is never treated as evidence.

**What it did to the router:** skill 12.63→11.40°, gate 23.01→22.59°, Cruise demand 8.01→7.02°, Send It 11.02→9.71°. Everything moved down, which is exactly what re-pricing at legal speed should do.

**Temperature: tested, did not replicate.** spearman(lean, temp) = −0.016 over 5,253 corners; per-trip +0.224 at p=0.24 (n=29). Direction right, magnitude undetectable. So `mu_for_temp` ships as a **labelled engineering assumption feeding the safety readout only** — never the fun score. I won't let anyone claim our data validates it.

Two things worth knowing: the fetch took ~15 min against rate-limited public mirrors (one, `private.coffee`, is dead — dropped), and I had a sign bug in my own console output that I caught and fixed. And on NDA: the query box is **rounded outward** to generic southern Bavaria, so not even the boundary we asked Overpass about is derived from BMW rides.

Full record in `docs/15_OSM_LAYER.md`.

---

Next up is **#2, the X-hour loop** — half the problem statement, currently zero. Shall I start it?

    """
    Make the edges already used expensive, in BOTH directions, so the return
    leg looks for another road. Riding the same pass back the way you came is
    a legal loop and a poor one.
    """
    m2 = m.copy()

            lo, hi = m2.indptr[a], m2.indptr[a + 1]
            k = np.flatnonzero(m2.indices[lo:hi] == b)
            if len(k):
                m2.data[lo + k[0]] *= factor
    return m2


def route_loop(start, hours: float, rider: Rider, z_star: float,
               graph: Graph | None = None,
               cells: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
               edges: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
               lam: float = LAMBDA_DEFAULT,
               tau: float = TAU_DEFAULT,
               osm: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
               tolerance: float = 0.20,
               n_candidates: int = 24,
               reuse_penalty: float = 6.0) -> Route:
    """
    BMW use case B: "give me a loop for the next X hours from here."

    Choosing the best closed tour under a time budget is the orienteering
    problem, which is NP-hard, so this is a heuristic — and an honest one:

      1. Dijkstra out from the start, and a second Dijkstra on the transposed
         graph, which gives the time to get BACK from every node. A node is a
         feasible turnaround only if out + back fits inside the budget.
      2. Rank the feasible ring by fit cost per second — low cost per second
         is exactly "this direction is full of roads that suit you".
      3. For the best handful, ride out to the turnaround, then make every
         edge just used 6x expensive and route home again. The return leg
         then finds different roads instead of retracing the outbound one.
      4. Keep the loops that land inside the budget and return the one with
         the best peak-end score.

    Time comes from the edge table's own median speeds, so the budget is in
    real riding minutes, not an assumed average.
    """
    cells = load_cells() if cells is None else cells
    edges = load_edges() if edges is None else edges
    if graph is None:
        graph = build_graph(edges, cells, rider, z_star, tau=tau, lam=lam, osm=osm)

    if not in_coverage(start[0], start[1]):
        return Route(False, note=(
            f"That start is outside BMW's coverage "
            f"({COVERAGE[0]}-{COVERAGE[1]} N, {COVERAGE[2]}-{COVERAGE[3]} E). "
            "We have no crowd there, so we have no opinion."))

    a = snap(start[0], start[1], cells, nodes=graph.nodes)
    si = graph.index[a]
    budget = float(hours) * 3600.0

    fit = graph.matrix
    sec = csr_matrix((_csr_aligned(graph, "seconds"), fit.indices, fit.indptr),
                     shape=fit.shape)

    t_out = dijkstra(sec, directed=True, indices=si)
    t_back = dijkstra(sec.T.tocsr(), directed=True, indices=si)
    c_out = dijkstra(fit, directed=True, indices=si)
    c_back = dijkstra(fit.T.tocsr(), directed=True, indices=si)

    total_t = t_out + t_back
    total_c = c_out + c_back
    # leave room for the detour the disjoint return will cost us
    feasible = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(total_t) & np.isfinite(total_c) &
                              (total_t >= 0.55 * budget) &
                              (total_t <= 0.95 * budget))
    if not len(feasible):
        reach = np.nanmax(t_out[np.isfinite(t_out)]) / 3600.0 if np.isfinite(t_out).any() else 0.0
        return Route(False, note=(
            f"No turnaround fits a {hours:.1f} h budget from here. The "
            f"furthest point reachable on roads we have data for is "
            f"{reach:.1f} h away, so try a shorter loop or a start with more "
            f"road around it."))

    order = feasible[np.argsort(total_c[feasible] / np.maximum(total_t[feasible], 1.0))]
    best, best_score = None, -1.0

    for mid in order[:n_candidates]:
        out_idx = _shortest(graph, si, int(mid))
        if out_idx is None or len(out_idx) < 2:
            continue
        used = list(zip(out_idx[:-1], out_idx[1:]))
        home_idx = _shortest(graph, int(mid), si,
                             matrix=_penalise(fit, used, reuse_penalty))
        if home_idx is None or len(home_idx) < 2:
            continue

        idx = out_idx + home_idx[1:]
        r = _assemble(graph, idx)
        if not r.ok:
            continue
        mins = r.summary["minutes"]
        if not (1.0 - tolerance) * hours * 60 <= mins <= (1.0 + tolerance) * hours * 60:
            continue
        # a loop that retraces itself is not a loop
        r.summary["distinct_share"] = len(set(r.cells)) / max(len(r.cells), 1)
        score = r.summary["fun_score"] * r.summary["distinct_share"]
        if score > best_score:
            best, best_score = r, score

    if best is None:
        return Route(False, note=(
            f"Found turnarounds for a {hours:.1f} h loop but none came home "
            f"inside the budget. Widen the tolerance or pick a start with "
            f"more connected road around it."))

    best.summary["is_loop"] = True
    best.summary["budget_min"] = hours * 60.0
    best.summary["turnaround"] = str(graph.nodes[order[0]])
    best.note = (best.note + " " if best.note else "") + (
        f"Loop: {best.summary['distinct_share']:.0%} of the cells are ridden "
        f"once, the rest is unavoidable retracing.")
    return best

"""
service.py — the one module the UI talks to.

Everything above this line is physics and graphs. Everything below it is
pixels. The UI never sees a DataFrame, never builds a graph, never knows what
a morton code is: it asks for a route and gets plain dicts and lists of
[lon, lat] pairs that go straight into pydeck.

Two reasons that matters tonight. It makes the front end assembly rather than
engineering, and it means the demo can run off a baked pickle with no BMW data
on the machine at all — `init()` will take the bake if it is there and fall
back to the parquets if it is not.

Typical use:

    import service as S
    S.init()
    S.riders()                       -> [{key, label, skill, sigma, gate, ...}]
    S.presets()                      -> {"routes": [...], "loops": [...]}
    S.route(A, B, "userA", 0.9)      -> dict, map-ready
    S.loop((47.66, 11.35), 2.0, "userA", 0.5)
    S.basemap()                      -> grey road polylines, offline
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pickle
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import router as R                                            # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BAKE = ROOT / "data" / "cache" / "demo.pkl"

Z_PRESETS = {"Cruise": 0.15, "Flow": 0.50, "Send it": 0.90}

# measured in analysis/12_route_calibration.py — pairs where the dial actually
# changes the road. Free-click is allowed but these are what we rehearse.
PRESET_ROUTES = [
    {"key": "lenggries_bad_toelz", "label": "Lenggries -> Bad Tolz",
     "a": (47.59, 11.75), "b": (47.73, 11.37),
     "why": "the strongest dial effect measured: 17% shared cells, +3 deg demand"},
    {"key": "lenggries_kochel", "label": "Lenggries -> Kochel",
     "a": (47.59, 11.75), "b": (47.73, 11.18), "why": "25% shared cells"},
    {"key": "kochel_tegernsee", "label": "Kochel -> Tegernsee",
     "a": (47.66, 11.35), "b": (47.85, 11.85), "why": "a genuine second corridor exists"},
]

PRESET_LOOPS = [
    {"key": "kochel", "label": "Kochel am See", "start": (47.66, 11.35)},
    {"key": "holzkirchen", "label": "Holzkirchen", "start": (47.90, 11.40)},
    {"key": "schliersee", "label": "Schliersee", "start": (47.85, 11.85)},
    {"key": "lenggries", "label": "Lenggries", "start": (47.59, 11.75)},
]

_S: dict | None = None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# startup
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def init(bake: Path | None = None, force_parquet: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Load once. Returns a small dict describing what was loaded."""
    global _S
    t0 = time.time()
    bake = Path(bake) if bake else BAKE

    if bake.exists() and not force_parquet:
        with open(bake, "rb") as f:
            d = pickle.load(f)
        _S = {**d, "graphs": {}, "source": f"bake {bake.name}"}
    else:
        cells = R.load_cells()
        osm = R.load_osm()
        cells = R.apply_legal_speed(cells, osm)
        _S = {"cells": cells, "edges": R.load_edges(), "osm": osm,
              "riders": _build_riders(cells), "basemap": None,
              "precomputed": {}, "graphs": {}, "source": "parquet"}

    _S["loaded_s"] = time.time() - t0
    return status()


def status() -> dict:
    s = _need()
    return {"source": s["source"], "loaded_s": round(s["loaded_s"], 3),
            "cells": len(s["cells"]), "edges": len(s["edges"]),
            "riders": len(s["riders"]), "osm": s["osm"] is not None,
            "basemap_ways": (len(s["basemap"]) if s.get("basemap") else 0),
            "precomputed": len(s.get("precomputed", {}))}


def _need() -> dict:
    if _S is None:
        init()
    return _S


def _build_riders(cells: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Calibrate every rider profile we can offer. Needs the corner table."""
    import flowstate as F
    corners = F.load_corners(filtered=True)
    out = {}
    r = R.calibrate_rider(corners, cells, "User A - all rides")
    out["userA"] = {"rider": r, "n_corners": int(len(corners)),
                    "grip_p95": R.rider_grip_p95(corners)}
    # User A rode 15 bikes. Lean p95 on an S1000RR and an R18 are not the same
    # measurement, so the honest "second rider" is the same human on a
    # different machine.
    for bike, n in corners["bike"].value_counts().head(2).items():
        sub = corners[corners["bike"] == bike]
        key = f"bike_{bike[:8]}"
        out[key] = {"rider": R.calibrate_rider(sub, cells, f"Bike {bike[:8]}"),
                    "n_corners": int(n), "grip_p95": R.rider_grip_p95(sub)}
    return out


def riders() -> list[dict]:
    s = _need()
    out = []
    for k, v in s["riders"].items():
        r = v["rider"]
        out.append({"key": k, "label": r.label, "skill": round(r.skill, 2),
                    "sigma": round(r.sigma, 2), "gate": round(r.gate, 2),
                    "hardest_ridden": round(float(r.hardest_ridden), 2),
                    "gate_agreement": round(float(r.gate_agreement), 3),
                    "n_cells": r.n_cells, "n_corners": v["n_corners"],
                    "grip_p95": round(float(v["grip_p95"]), 2)})
    return out


def presets() -> dict:
    return {"routes": PRESET_ROUTES, "loops": PRESET_LOOPS, "dial": Z_PRESETS}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# graphs, cached per (rider, dial)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _graph(rider_key: str, z_star: float, lam: float = R.LAMBDA_DEFAULT):
    s = _need()
    key = (rider_key, round(float(z_star), 3), round(float(lam), 2))
    if key not in s["graphs"]:
        if len(s["graphs"]) > 12:               # keep the dial responsive, not greedy
            s["graphs"].clear()
        s["graphs"][key] = R.build_graph(
            s["edges"], s["cells"], s["riders"][rider_key]["rider"],
            float(z_star), lam=lam, osm=s["osm"])
    return s["graphs"][key]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the two answers BMW asked for
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def route(a, b, rider_key: str = "userA", z_star: float = 0.5,
          lam: float = R.LAMBDA_DEFAULT) -> dict:
    """A -> B. Everything the map and the caption need, in plain types."""
    s = _need()
    g = _graph(rider_key, z_star, lam)
    r = R.route_a_to_b(tuple(a), tuple(b), s["riders"][rider_key]["rider"],
                       float(z_star), graph=g, cells=s["cells"],
                       edges=s["edges"], osm=s["osm"], lam=lam)
    return _pack(r, g, rider_key, z_star)


def loop(start, hours: float, rider_key: str = "userA",
         z_star: float = 0.5, lam: float = R.LAMBDA_DEFAULT) -> dict:
    """A closed loop of roughly `hours` from `start`."""
    s = _need()
    g = _graph(rider_key, z_star, lam)
    r = R.route_loop(tuple(start), float(hours),
                     s["riders"][rider_key]["rider"], float(z_star),
                     graph=g, cells=s["cells"], edges=s["edges"],
                     osm=s["osm"], lam=lam)
    return _pack(r, g, rider_key, z_star)


def compare(a, b, rider_key: str = "userA",
            lo: float = 0.15, hi: float = 0.90) -> dict:
    """
    The money shot: the same A and B at two dial settings, side by side.
    Do not make a judge drag a slider and hope — show both at once.
    """
    x, y = route(a, b, rider_key, lo), route(a, b, rider_key, hi)
    out = {"low": x, "high": y, "lo_z": lo, "hi_z": hi}
    if x["ok"] and y["ok"]:
        ca, cb = set(x["cells"]), set(y["cells"])
        out["overlap"] = len(ca & cb) / max(len(ca | cb), 1)
        out["km_ratio"] = y["summary"]["km"] / max(x["summary"]["km"], 1e-9)
        out["demand_gain"] = (y["summary"]["mean_demand"]
                              - x["summary"]["mean_demand"])
        out["headline"] = (
            f"Same two points. {out['km_ratio']:.2f}x the distance, "
            f"{1-out['overlap']:.0%} of it on different roads, "
            f"{out['demand_gain']:+.1f} deg more lean asked of you.")
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# packing — the only place that knows what pydeck wants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _pack(r, g, rider_key: str, z_star: float) -> dict:
    if not r.ok:
        return {"ok": False, "note": r.note, "path": [], "segments": [],
                "refusals": [], "summary": {}, "explain": [r.note]}

    sc = g.scored
    on = sc.reindex(r.cells)
    path = [[float(lo), float(la)]
            for la, lo in zip(on["lat"].to_numpy(), on["lon"].to_numpy())
            if np.isfinite(la) and np.isfinite(lo)]

    flow = np.nan_to_num(on["flow"].to_numpy(dtype=float))
    dem = np.nan_to_num(on["demand"].to_numpy(dtype=float))
    segments = [{"from": path[i], "to": path[i + 1],
                 "flow": float(flow[i + 1]), "demand": float(dem[i + 1])}
                for i in range(len(path) - 1)]

    summary = {k: (float(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float, np.floating)) else v)
               for k, v in r.summary.items() if k != "refusals"}
    return {"ok": True, "note": r.note, "cells": list(r.cells), "path": path,
            "segments": segments, "refusals": r.summary.get("refusals", []),
            "summary": summary, "rider": rider_key, "z_star": float(z_star),
            "explain": explain(summary, r.summary.get("refusals", []),
                               _need()["riders"][rider_key]["rider"], z_star)}


def explain(summary: dict, refusals: list, rider, z_star: float) -> list[str]:
    """
    Sentences a human can read out. Explainability is a judged criterion, so
    the reasons live next to the numbers rather than in a slide.
    """
    out = []
    if summary.get("is_loop"):
        out.append(f"A {summary['km']:.0f} km loop back to where you started, "
                   f"{summary['minutes']:.0f} minutes of riding against the "
                   f"{summary['budget_min']:.0f} you asked for.")
        if summary.get("distinct_share", 1) < 0.95:
            out.append(f"{summary['distinct_share']:.0%} of it is road you only "
                       f"ride once; the rest is unavoidable retracing.")
    else:
        out.append(f"{summary['km']:.0f} km, about {summary['minutes']:.0f} "
                   f"minutes.")

    out.append(f"This road asks a mean {summary['mean_demand']:.1f} deg of lean "
               f"and peaks at {summary['max_demand']:.1f} deg. Your gate is "
               f"{rider.gate:.1f} deg, which is 2 sigma above the road you "
               f"habitually ride.")
    out.append(f"Best five kilometres score {summary['peak_flow']:.2f} out of 1 "
               f"for fit at this dial setting.")
    if summary.get("grip_lat_p95") == summary.get("grip_lat_p95"):
        out.append(f"Cornering grip used peaks around "
                   f"{summary['grip_lat_p95']:.0%} of what the tyre has, "
                   f"against the {0:.0f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".") +
                   f"")
    if refusals:
        out.append(f"{len(refusals)} road(s) near this route were refused "
                   f"outright, not just made expensive:")
        out += [f"    {x['reason']}" for x in refusals[:3]]
    else:
        out.append("Nothing on this route crosses your safety gate.")
    if summary.get("imputed_cells"):
        out.append(f"{int(summary['imputed_cells'])} cells had no corner in the "
                   f"crowd data and were treated as straight, not as missing.")
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# offline basemap
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def basemap() -> list:
    """
    Grey road polylines from the cached OSM tiles, so the map has context with
    the network unplugged. Built at bake time; None means fall back to tiles.
    """
    return _need().get("basemap") or []


def cells_layer(rider_key: str = "userA", z_star: float = 0.5,
                min_flow: float = 0.0) -> list:
    """Every scored cell, for colouring the map by fit."""
    g = _graph(rider_key, z_star)
    sc = g.scored
    m = sc["flow"].to_numpy(dtype=float) >= min_flow
    sub = sc[m]
    return [{"lat": float(a), "lon": float(o), "flow": float(f),
             "demand": float(d), "gated": bool(x)}
            for a, o, f, d, x in zip(sub["lat"], sub["lon"], sub["flow"],
                                     sub["demand"], sub["gated"])]

content.text:
Pausing there — `service.py` is written but **not yet tested or committed**, so treat it as in-flight.

Here's what the engine can actually do today.

## The two answers BMW asked for

**1. A→B route chosen by fit, not distance** — 60 ms
Costs every road by how well it suits *this* rider at *this* dial setting, not by how fast it gets you there.

**2. X-hour loop from a start point** — 150 ms
Closed tour, returns to where you started, fills 80–112% of the time you asked for, 86–100% of it road you ride only once. 16/16 start × duration combinations work.

## The Thrill Dial

One control changes what "good road" means — Cruise (0.15) / Flow (0.50) / Send it (0.90). Same two points, and the router hands back **83% different roads** asking **+3° more lean**. It doesn't pad your mileage; it changes the character of the ride.

## Rider DNA

Skill and spread measured from the rider's own corners, calibrated onto the same axis the road demand lives on. Supports **User A plus per-bike profiles** — same human on an S1000RR vs an R18 is genuinely a different rider, and the model shows it.

## Safety, and this is the strongest part

- **A hard gate that refuses, not penalises.** A road past skill + 2σ is *removed from the graph*. You can't buy past it with a big enough detour budget.
- **The gate lands where it should without being told to** — within 3–6% of the hardest road that rider has actually ridden, independently, at two different cell sizes.
- **Every refusal comes with a sentence**: *"the crowd leans 24° here, past your gate of 23°."*
- **Friction circle** — grip used, lateral and longitudinal together, against the rider's own demonstrated 1.04 envelope.

## Never recommending speeding — as a mechanism, not a promise

On half the roads where OSM knows the limit, the crowd's p85 exceeds it. So demand is **recomputed at the posted speed** (`tan θ ∝ v²`), dropping those cells 9.67° → 5.60°. A road still competes — on what it *legally* offers.

## BMW's own flags, as facts

🔴 motorway/trunk · 🔴 residential/living-street · 🔴 unpaved/cobbled · 🟢 country road — from OSM tags, not guessed from telemetry.

## Scoring

**Peak-end fun score**: 35% mean + 40% best-5-km + 25% final-15%, minus a dull-tail penalty. Because what you remember about a ride is the best bit and the end, not the average.

## Underneath

import json
import pickle
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "app"))

import router as R          # noqa: E402
import service as S         # noqa: E402

OUT = ROOT / "data" / "cache" / "demo.pkl"
OSM_CACHE = ROOT / "data" / "osm"

# only the roads worth drawing as context — residential clutters the map and
# triples the file
BASEMAP_CLASSES = {"motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary", "tertiary",
                   "unclassified", "motorway_link", "trunk_link"}
SIMPLIFY_M = 60.0          # drop basemap vertices closer together than this


def build_basemap() -> list:
    """Road polylines from the cached OSM tiles, simplified for drawing."""
    out = []
    for p in sorted(OSM_CACHE.glob("tile_*.json")):
        for el in json.loads(p.read_bytes()).get("elements", []):
            if el.get("tags", {}).get("highway") not in BASEMAP_CLASSES:
                continue
            g = el.get("geometry") or []
            if len(g) < 2:
                continue
            la = np.fromiter((x["lat"] for x in g), float)
            lo = np.fromiter((x["lon"] for x in g), float)
            keep = [0]
            for k in range(1, len(la)):
                d = np.hypot((la[k] - la[keep[-1]]) * 110540.0,
                             (lo[k] - lo[keep[-1]]) * 74000.0)
                if d >= SIMPLIFY_M or k == len(la) - 1:
                    keep.append(k)
            if len(keep) < 2:
                continue
            out.append({"cls": el["tags"]["highway"],
                        "path": [[round(float(lo[k]), 5), round(float(la[k]), 5)]
                                 for k in keep]})
    return out

    print("[3] basemap from cached OSM tiles")
    basemap = build_basemap()
    print(f"    {len(basemap):,} ways, "

    print("[4] pre-solving the presets")
    payload = {"cells": cells, "edges": edges, "osm": osm, "riders": riders,

    S._S = {**payload, "graphs": {}, "source": "bake(build)",

    pre = {}
    for p in S.PRESET_ROUTES:

            pre[f"route:{p['key']}:{z}"] = r

    for p in S.PRESET_LOOPS:

                  f"{r['summary'].get('km', 0):6.1f} km")

    print(f"  {len(pre)} pre-solved answers, {len(basemap):,} basemap ways")

Working well — **12 ms load from bake**, 20–37 ms per dial change. But there's a real correctness bug in the output:

> *"Cornering asks about 33% of the tyre's grip, against the **104%** you have already used"*

You cannot use 104% of available grip. The cause: I'm combining each corner's **peak lean** with its **peak braking** — but those happen at *different moments*. A friction circle needs simultaneous values.

    assumes a simultaneity the data does not show, and the corner table has no
    per-sample pairing to recover it.

    So we report the honest half: lateral grip, sqrt(tan(theta)^2)/mu, which
    is exactly the basis the route summary uses for `grip_lat_p95`. The two
    numbers are then comparable, which is the point of showing them together.

    g = grip_used(corners["lean_deg"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, mu=mu)
    g = g[np.isfinite(g)]
    return float(np.percentile(g, 95)) if len(g) else float("nan")

The half of BMW's brief we had not answered at all. Choosing the best closed
tour under a time budget is the orienteering problem, which is NP-hard, so
this is a heuristic and says so out loud:

1. Dijkstra out from the start, and a second one on the **transposed** graph
   for the time to get *back*. A node is a feasible turnaround only if
   out + back fits the budget.
2. Rank that ring by **fit cost per second** — a low cost per second is
   exactly "this direction is full of roads that suit this rider".
3. Ride out, make every edge just used **6x** expensive, and route home
   again, so the return leg finds different roads instead of retracing.
4. Keep the loops inside budget; pick the best by
   `flow x distinctness x how well it fills the time asked for`.

riding minutes, not an assumed average.

54	basemap() cells_layer() status()
55	```
56	
57	`compare(A, B)` is the demo's money shot and writes its own headline:
58	
59	> Same two points. 1.13x the distance, 83% of it on different roads,
60	> +2.7 deg more lean asked of you.
61	
62	Show both dial settings at once. **Do not make a judge drag a slider and
63	hope** — across 200 O-D pairs the median demand gain is -0.00 deg, so on a
64	randomly clicked pair nothing visible happens (doc 14).
65	
66	`explain()` returns sentences, not numbers, because explainability is judged
67	and the reason belongs beside the answer:
68	
69	```
70	This road asks a mean 9.7 deg of lean and peaks at 22.4 deg. Your gate is
71	22.6 deg, which is 2 sigma above the road you habitually ride.
72	Cornering asks about 33% of the tyre's grip here, against the 53% you have
73	already used on your own rides.
74	REFUSED - the crowd leans 24 deg here, past your gate of 23 deg (11 + 2 sigma).
75	```

77	## `data/cache/demo.pkl` — the freeze artefact
78	
79	**The repo cannot reproduce a demo on its own.** The lake and every derived
80	parquet are gitignored and stay on this Mac. `analysis/14_bake_demo.py` writes
81	the one file the app needs: scored cells, edges, the OSM join, calibrated
82	riders, a **17,345-way grey road basemap** for drawing with the network
83	unplugged, and 21 pre-solved preset answers.
84	
85	```
86	5.2 MB, built in 2.4 s
87	init() from the bake      12 ms
88	dial change            20-37 ms     <- live enough for a slider on a phone
89	loop                     146 ms
90	```
91	
92	Rebake after ANY change to the router, the cell table or the OSM layer.
93	
94	## Riders
95	
96	Three profiles. There is no user B in the data — only `exampleUserA` — but
97	User A rode 15 bikes, and lean p95 on an S1000RR and on an R18 are not the
98	same measurement. So the honest second rider is the same human on a different
99	machine:
100	
101	```
102	userA           skill 11.40  sigma 5.59  gate 22.59  agree 1.063x  grip 53%
103	bike_da67fa06   skill 10.10  sigma 6.57  gate 23.25  agree 0.901x  grip 48%
104	bike_4e1a9d64   skill 13.25  sigma 5.32  gate 23.89  agree 1.169x  grip 58%
105	```
106	
107	**Known weakness: switching rider does not change the route** on the preset
108	pairs — all three return 53.0 km with identical mean demand. Not a caching
109	bug; their gates differ but none bites on that road, and with one corridor per
110	O-D pair the same path wins for everyone. **Frame the rider switch around the
111	numbers (gate, grip, skill), not the line on the map**, or find a pair where
112	the gate actually bites.
113	
114	## The grip bug, and why it matters
115	
116	Rider grip utilisation was being reported as **104% of available grip**. That
117	is not a hard rider, it is a bug: it combined each corner's peak lean with
118	that corner's peak |a_long|, and those happen at different instants — you
119	brake hard upright on the way in and lean hard off the brakes at the apex. The
120	corner table has no per-sample pairing to recover simultaneity.
121	
122	Now reports **lateral only**, on exactly the same basis as the route's
123	`grip_lat_p95`, so the two are comparable: rider 53%, this route 33%. The
124	longitudinal term stays in `grip_used` for anywhere we do have simultaneous
125	samples.
126	
127	## Reproducing

1	# 14 — Phase 2: the router
2	
3	Written 2026-09-13 on the Mac. Everything here was measured by
4	`analysis/12_route_calibration.py`, which reruns in ~18 s.
5	
6	`app/router.py` is done and runs a full A→B route in **60 ms**. Four
7	functions as specified: `build_graph`, `snap`, `route_a_to_b`,
8	`route_summary`, plus `calibrate_rider` and `compare_routes`, which the plan
9	did not anticipate needing and which turned out to be the whole job.
10	
11	## The plan's stop-check cannot be met, and that is a finding
12	
13	Phase 2 ends with: tune LAMBDA until Send It is 1.5–1.8× the direct distance.
14	**The maximum detour available anywhere in this network is 1.137×.** Not a
15	tuning problem — three independent measurements say the graph has no room:
16	
17	**1. LAMBDA has a mathematical ceiling.** `cost = L·(1 + λ(1−flow))` tends to
18	`λ·L·(1−flow)` as λ grows, so above some λ the *ranking* of paths cannot
19	change. Measured: λ = 3, 6, 10, 20, 40, 80 return the byte-identical route.
20	λ is not a dial you can keep turning.
21	
22	**2. At 18 characters there is exactly one corridor.** Delete the shortest
23	path's edges and ask again:
24	
25	```
26	_s2  Bad Tolz -> Tegernsee    30.4 km / 285 cells | 2nd disjoint path: NONE, disconnected
27	_s2  Kochel -> Tegernsee      52.8 km / 499 cells | 2nd disjoint path: NONE, disconnected
28	_s2  Starnberg -> Schliersee  66.1 km / 610 cells | 2nd disjoint path: NONE, disconnected
29	```
30	
31	A graph built from 8,000 ride traces at 153×102 m is a **bundle of corridors,
32	not a road network**. Riders follow the same roads; the branches between them
33	were never ridden, so they do not exist. No cost function of any shape can
34	route around something that has no second path.
35	
36	**3. So the router runs at 16 characters.** ~600×400 m cells let parallel
37	roads share a node and real alternatives appear:
38	
39	```
40	_c16 Bad Tolz -> Tegernsee    30.7 km /  75 cells | 2nd disjoint: 41.5 km (1.35x)
41	_c16 Kochel -> Tegernsee      53.6 km / 130 cells | 2nd disjoint: 74.2 km (1.38x)
42	_c16 Starnberg -> Schliersee  54.9 km / 140 cells | 2nd disjoint: NONE
43	```
44	
45	**This reverses doc 13's "staying at CELL_CHARS=18" — for routing only.**
46	Doc 13 was right that mean out-degree is a bad reason to coarsen, and it
47	tested degree. Degree was the wrong metric for a router. The right one is
48	whether a second corridor exists, and at 18 chars it does not, anywhere.
49	Scoring, the map, and the corner work stay at 18. **Only topology moves.**
50	
51	The cost: a 600×400 m cell can fuse two genuinely separate roads into one
52	node. Edges still come only from real ride transitions, so no edge is
53	invented — but a false junction is possible where two roads pass within
54	600 m. In alpine valleys they usually do connect. This is a real risk and
55	should be said aloud rather than hidden.
56	
57	## Two bugs found in the Phase 1 output
58	
59	**`median_metres` is not edge length.** It is the distance between the last
60	sample before a cell boundary and the first sample after it — two samples one
61	second apart, ~21 m at 75 km/h. A cell is 153 m across. Summing it gave
62	**10.1 km for a route whose endpoints are 42.8 km apart**. The router now
63	computes length as the haversine distance between cell centres and derives
64	time from `length / median_speed`. `median_seconds` (always ≈1.0 s) is the
65	same artefact and is not used. *`graph_edges` itself is unchanged — the fix
66	lives in the consumer.*
67	
68	**`10_crowd_layer.py` never read `FS_CELL_CHARS`.** It hardcoded
69	`CELL_CHARS = 18` while script 11 honoured the variable, so asking for a
70	16-char build produced an 18-char cell table and a 16-char edge table that
71	could not be joined. Doc 13 states this variable works; it only ever worked
72	for script 11. **Fixed.**
73	
74	## The scale mismatch that made every road score zero
75	
76	The first working router scored flow ≈ 0 on all 21,130 cells. The cause was
77	not code:
78	
79	- `rider_dna` skill = peak lean **per corner**, p95 = **30.2°**
80	- `demand_p90` = 90th percentile over **every sample in a cell**, straights
81	  included, median **7.4°**
82	
83	Different statistics of the same physical quantity. Subtracting one from the
84	other gives z ≈ −3 everywhere and the model says "nothing in Bavaria could
85	interest you" — an artefact of aggregation, not a fact about the rider.
86	
87	`calibrate_rider` fixes it by measuring the rider with the crowd's own ruler:
88	take the cells this rider actually rode, and read skill off the same
89	`demand_p90` column the challenge comes from. Skill is the **median** of
90	those cells, not p95 — `z = (challenge − skill)/σ` is a stretch measured from
91	where the rider normally lives, so z* = 0 has to mean "the road I habitually
92	ride".
93	
94	### The gate lands on the hardest road actually ridden
95	
96	Nothing in the construction forces this, and it holds at both resolutions:
97	
98	| grid | skill (median) | σ | gate = skill + 2σ | p95 of ridden cells | ratio |
99	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
100	| 18 chars | 14.68° | 6.31° | **27.29°** | 26.62° | **1.025×** |
101	| 16 chars | 12.63° | 5.19° | **23.01°** | 23.18° | **0.992×** |
102	
103	A safety threshold derived from the *spread* of this rider's road choices
104	lands within 3% of the hardest road they have ever chosen — derived
105	independently, at two different cell sizes. This is the best evidence we have
106	that the gate is set at a real place, and it is the strongest single number
107	Phase 2 produced.
108	
109	## What the dial actually moves
110	
111	200 routable O-D pairs, 25–75 km apart, λ=10:
112	
113	```
114	detour ratio : median 1.005   p90 1.055   MAX 1.137
115	cell overlap : p10 0.255      median 0.881
116	demand gain  : median -0.00 deg   p90 +0.75 deg
117	```
118	
119	**Read the median honestly: for a typical pair of points the dial does
120	almost nothing.** The effect is real but concentrated in a minority of pairs
121	— the ones with a genuine alternative corridor. A judge who clicks two random
122	points will very likely see the same road twice. Phase 6's rehearsed start
123	points are therefore not stagecraft, they are a requirement.
124	
125	Where it does work, it works well. The best pair in the network:
126	
127	```
128	(47.59, 11.75) -> (47.73, 11.37)      direct 46.9 km
129	  Cruise  z*=0.15   47.0 km / 44 min   1.00x   mean demand  8.01 deg   peak flow 0.499
130	  Send it z*=0.90   53.3 km / 41 min   1.14x   mean demand 11.02 deg   peak flow 0.560
131	  dial effect: 1.13x the distance, 17% of cells shared, +3.01 deg mean demand
132	```
133	
134	**The honest headline is not "we ride you further". It is: for the same two
135	points and roughly the same distance, the dial puts you on 83% different
136	roads, 38% more demanding.** That is a better claim than the plan's anyway —
137	it says the router is choosing character, not padding mileage.
138	
139	## Safety, as measured
140	
141	- Gate refuses **256 of 10,318 edges** at this rider's setting, and the graph
142	  stays connected (LCC 97.1% at 16 chars) — the fallback that reopens the
143	  gate as a penalty did not fire on any of the 200 scanned pairs.
144	- A refusal is a removed edge, not an expensive one. A safety gate you can
145	  buy past with a big enough detour budget is not a gate.
146	- Friction circle: `grip = sqrt(tan(theta)² + (a_long/g)²)/mu`, mu = 1.1.
147	  `a_long` is already in g (doc 13) — it is **not** divided by 9.81 again.
148	  Rider's own p95 = **1.04**; the Cruise route asks 0.23 and Send It 0.33
149	  (lateral only). Both routes sit far inside this rider's demonstrated
150	  envelope.
151	- `a_min`/`a_max` are clipped at 1.0 g before the grip percentile; the raw
152	  columns reach −2.6 g, which is not a motorcycle.
153	
154	## Things the UI must not get wrong
155	
156	- **`fun_score` is comparable across routes at the same dial, never across
157	  dial settings.** Flow is fit to whatever z* is asked for, so Send It can
158	  score *below* Cruise on the same roads (it does: 22.4 vs 25.4) without
159	  either being wrong. Show the dial next to the number, or compare
160	  `mean_demand`, which is absolute.
161	- Start and finish outside the coverage box return a refusal with a reason,
162	  not an empty map. **A Zürich start still returns nothing** — bound the map.
163	- Edges are **symmetrised**. `graph_edges` is directed by ride direction, so
164	  a road only ever caught northbound had no southbound edge; that is a fact
165	  about the sample, not the road. This does reverse genuine one-way streets,
166	  which is rare outside town centres and is the cheaper error.
167	
168	## Reproducing

177	FS_CELL_CHARS=16 $V analysis/11_build_graph.py --set trips-samples-2 --tag _c16
178	$V app/router.py                      # the stop-check, 60 ms per route
179	$V analysis/12_route_calibration.py   # all the evidence above, ~18 s

"""
service.py — the one module the UI talks to.

Everything above this line is physics and graphs. Everything below it is
pixels. The UI never sees a DataFrame, never builds a graph, never knows what
a morton code is: it asks for a route and gets plain dicts and lists of
[lon, lat] pairs that go straight into pydeck.

Two reasons that matters tonight. It makes the front end assembly rather than
engineering, and it means the demo can run off a baked pickle with no BMW data
on the machine at all — `init()` will take the bake if it is there and fall
back to the parquets if it is not.

Typical use:

    import service as S
    S.init()
    S.riders()                       -> [{key, label, skill, sigma, gate, ...}]
    S.presets()                      -> {"routes": [...], "loops": [...]}
    S.route(A, B, "userA", 0.9)      -> dict, map-ready
    S.loop((47.66, 11.35), 2.0, "userA", 0.5)
    S.basemap()                      -> grey road polylines, offline
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pickle
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import router as R                                            # noqa: E402

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BAKE = ROOT / "data" / "cache" / "demo.pkl"

Z_PRESETS = {"Cruise": 0.15, "Flow": 0.50, "Send it": 0.90}

# measured in analysis/12_route_calibration.py — pairs where the dial actually
# changes the road. Free-click is allowed but these are what we rehearse.
PRESET_ROUTES = [
    {"key": "lenggries_bad_toelz", "label": "Lenggries -> Bad Tolz",
     "a": (47.59, 11.75), "b": (47.73, 11.37),
     "why": "the strongest dial effect measured: 17% shared cells, +3 deg demand"},
    {"key": "lenggries_kochel", "label": "Lenggries -> Kochel",
     "a": (47.59, 11.75), "b": (47.73, 11.18), "why": "25% shared cells"},
    {"key": "kochel_tegernsee", "label": "Kochel -> Tegernsee",
     "a": (47.66, 11.35), "b": (47.85, 11.85), "why": "a genuine second corridor exists"},
]

PRESET_LOOPS = [
    {"key": "kochel", "label": "Kochel am See", "start": (47.66, 11.35)},
    {"key": "holzkirchen", "label": "Holzkirchen", "start": (47.90, 11.40)},
    {"key": "schliersee", "label": "Schliersee", "start": (47.85, 11.85)},
    {"key": "lenggries", "label": "Lenggries", "start": (47.59, 11.75)},
]

_S: dict | None = None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# startup
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def init(bake: Path | None = None, force_parquet: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Load once. Returns a small dict describing what was loaded."""
    global _S
    t0 = time.time()
    bake = Path(bake) if bake else BAKE

    if bake.exists() and not force_parquet:
        with open(bake, "rb") as f:
            d = pickle.load(f)
        _S = {**d, "graphs": {}, "source": f"bake {bake.name}"}
    else:
        cells = R.load_cells()
        osm = R.load_osm()
        cells = R.apply_legal_speed(cells, osm)
        _S = {"cells": cells, "edges": R.load_edges(), "osm": osm,
              "riders": _build_riders(cells), "basemap": None,
              "precomputed": {}, "graphs": {}, "source": "parquet"}

    _S["loaded_s"] = time.time() - t0
    return status()


def status() -> dict:
    s = _need()
    return {"source": s["source"], "loaded_s": round(s["loaded_s"], 3),
            "cells": len(s["cells"]), "edges": len(s["edges"]),
            "riders": len(s["riders"]), "osm": s["osm"] is not None,
            "basemap_ways": (len(s["basemap"]) if s.get("basemap") else 0),
            "precomputed": len(s.get("precomputed", {}))}


def _need() -> dict:
    if _S is None:
        init()
    return _S


def _build_riders(cells: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Calibrate every rider profile we can offer. Needs the corner table."""
    import flowstate as F
    corners = F.load_corners(filtered=True)
    out = {}
    r = R.calibrate_rider(corners, cells, "User A - all rides")
    out["userA"] = {"rider": r, "n_corners": int(len(corners)),
                    "grip_p95": R.rider_grip_p95(corners)}
    # User A rode 15 bikes. Lean p95 on an S1000RR and an R18 are not the same
    # measurement, so the honest "second rider" is the same human on a
    # different machine.
    for bike, n in corners["bike"].value_counts().head(2).items():
        sub = corners[corners["bike"] == bike]
        key = f"bike_{bike[:8]}"
        out[key] = {"rider": R.calibrate_rider(sub, cells, f"Bike {bike[:8]}"),
                    "n_corners": int(n), "grip_p95": R.rider_grip_p95(sub)}
    return out


def riders() -> list[dict]:
    s = _need()
    out = []
    for k, v in s["riders"].items():
        r = v["rider"]
        out.append({"key": k, "label": r.label, "skill": round(r.skill, 2),
                    "sigma": round(r.sigma, 2), "gate": round(r.gate, 2),
                    "hardest_ridden": round(float(r.hardest_ridden), 2),
                    "gate_agreement": round(float(r.gate_agreement), 3),
                    "n_cells": r.n_cells, "n_corners": v["n_corners"],
                    "grip_p95": round(float(v["grip_p95"]), 2)})
    return out


def presets() -> dict:
    return {"routes": PRESET_ROUTES, "loops": PRESET_LOOPS, "dial": Z_PRESETS}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# graphs, cached per (rider, dial)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _graph(rider_key: str, z_star: float, lam: float = R.LAMBDA_DEFAULT):
    s = _need()
    key = (rider_key, round(float(z_star), 3), round(float(lam), 2))
    if key not in s["graphs"]:
        if len(s["graphs"]) > 12:               # keep the dial responsive, not greedy
            s["graphs"].clear()
        s["graphs"][key] = R.build_graph(
            s["edges"], s["cells"], s["riders"][rider_key]["rider"],
            float(z_star), lam=lam, osm=s["osm"])
    return s["graphs"][key]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the two answers BMW asked for
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def route(a, b, rider_key: str = "userA", z_star: float = 0.5,
          lam: float = R.LAMBDA_DEFAULT) -> dict:
    """A -> B. Everything the map and the caption need, in plain types."""
    s = _need()
    g = _graph(rider_key, z_star, lam)
    r = R.route_a_to_b(tuple(a), tuple(b), s["riders"][rider_key]["rider"],
                       float(z_star), graph=g, cells=s["cells"],
                       edges=s["edges"], osm=s["osm"], lam=lam)
    return _pack(r, g, rider_key, z_star)


def loop(start, hours: float, rider_key: str = "userA",
         z_star: float = 0.5, lam: float = R.LAMBDA_DEFAULT) -> dict:
    """A closed loop of roughly `hours` from `start`."""
    s = _need()
    g = _graph(rider_key, z_star, lam)
    r = R.route_loop(tuple(start), float(hours),
                     s["riders"][rider_key]["rider"], float(z_star),
                     graph=g, cells=s["cells"], edges=s["edges"],
                     osm=s["osm"], lam=lam)
    return _pack(r, g, rider_key, z_star)


def compare(a, b, rider_key: str = "userA",
            lo: float = 0.15, hi: float = 0.90) -> dict:
    """
    The money shot: the same A and B at two dial settings, side by side.
    Do not make a judge drag a slider and hope — show both at once.
    """
    x, y = route(a, b, rider_key, lo), route(a, b, rider_key, hi)
    out = {"low": x, "high": y, "lo_z": lo, "hi_z": hi}
    if x["ok"] and y["ok"]:
        ca, cb = set(x["cells"]), set(y["cells"])
        out["overlap"] = len(ca & cb) / max(len(ca | cb), 1)
        out["km_ratio"] = y["summary"]["km"] / max(x["summary"]["km"], 1e-9)
        out["demand_gain"] = (y["summary"]["mean_demand"]
                              - x["summary"]["mean_demand"])
        out["headline"] = (
            f"Same two points. {out['km_ratio']:.2f}x the distance, "
            f"{1-out['overlap']:.0%} of it on different roads, "
            f"{out['demand_gain']:+.1f} deg more lean asked of you.")
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# packing — the only place that knows what pydeck wants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _pack(r, g, rider_key: str, z_star: float) -> dict:
    if not r.ok:
        return {"ok": False, "note": r.note, "path": [], "segments": [],
                "refusals": [], "summary": {}, "explain": [r.note]}

    sc = g.scored
    on = sc.reindex(r.cells)
    path = [[float(lo), float(la)]
            for la, lo in zip(on["lat"].to_numpy(), on["lon"].to_numpy())
            if np.isfinite(la) and np.isfinite(lo)]

    flow = np.nan_to_num(on["flow"].to_numpy(dtype=float))
    dem = np.nan_to_num(on["demand"].to_numpy(dtype=float))
    segments = [{"from": path[i], "to": path[i + 1],
                 "flow": float(flow[i + 1]), "demand": float(dem[i + 1])}
                for i in range(len(path) - 1)]

    summary = {k: (float(v) if isinstance(v, (int, float, np.floating)) else v)
               for k, v in r.summary.items() if k != "refusals"}
    return {"ok": True, "note": r.note, "cells": list(r.cells), "path": path,
            "segments": segments, "refusals": r.summary.get("refusals", []),
            "summary": summary, "rider": rider_key, "z_star": float(z_star),
            "explain": explain(summary, r.summary.get("refusals", []),
                               _need()["riders"][rider_key]["rider"], z_star,
                               _need()["riders"][rider_key]["grip_p95"])}


def explain(summary: dict, refusals: list, rider, z_star: float,
            rider_grip: float | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """
    Sentences a human can read out. Explainability is a judged criterion, so
    the reasons live next to the numbers rather than in a slide.
    """
    out = []
    if summary.get("is_loop"):
        out.append(f"A {summary['km']:.0f} km loop back to where you started, "
                   f"{summary['minutes']:.0f} minutes of riding against the "
                   f"{summary['budget_min']:.0f} you asked for.")
        if summary.get("distinct_share", 1) < 0.95:
            out.append(f"{summary['distinct_share']:.0%} of it is road you only "
                       f"ride once; the rest is unavoidable retracing.")
    else:
        out.append(f"{summary['km']:.0f} km, about {summary['minutes']:.0f} "
                   f"minutes.")

    out.append(f"This road asks a mean {summary['mean_demand']:.1f} deg of lean "
               f"and peaks at {summary['max_demand']:.1f} deg. Your gate is "
               f"{rider.gate:.1f} deg, which is 2 sigma above the road you "
               f"habitually ride.")
    out.append(f"Best five kilometres score {summary['peak_flow']:.2f} out of 1 "
               f"for fit at this dial setting.")
    grip = summary.get("grip_lat_p95")
    if grip is not None and np.isfinite(grip):
        msg = (f"Cornering asks about {grip:.0%} of the tyre's grip here")
        if rider_grip and np.isfinite(rider_grip):
            msg += (f", against the {rider_grip:.0%} you have already used on "
                    f"your own rides")
        out.append(msg + ".")
    if refusals:
        out.append(f"{len(refusals)} road(s) near this route were refused "
                   f"outright, not just made expensive:")
        out += [f"    {x['reason']}" for x in refusals[:3]]
    else:
        out.append("Nothing on this route crosses your safety gate.")
    if summary.get("imputed_cells"):
        out.append(f"{int(summary['imputed_cells'])} cells had no corner in the "
                   f"crowd data and were treated as straight, not as missing.")
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# offline basemap
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def basemap() -> list:
    """
    Grey road polylines from the cached OSM tiles, so the map has context with
    the network unplugged. Built at bake time; None means fall back to tiles.
    """
    return _need().get("basemap") or []


def cells_layer(rider_key: str = "userA", z_star: float = 0.5,
                min_flow: float = 0.0) -> list:
    """Every scored cell, for colouring the map by fit."""
    g = _graph(rider_key, z_star)
    sc = g.scored
    m = sc["flow"].to_numpy(dtype=float) >= min_flow
    sub = sc[m]
    return [{"lat": float(a), "lon": float(o), "flow": float(f),
             "demand": float(d), "gated": bool(x)}
            for a, o, f, d, x in zip(sub["lat"], sub["lon"], sub["flow"],
                                     sub["demand"], sub["gated"])]

    return len(at.get("deck_gl_json_chart"))

# 17 — Phase 3: the ROUTE tab

Written 2026-09-13 ~00:40 CEST on the Mac. This is the phase that turns a
finished backend into something a judge can click.

Before this, `streamlit_app.py` had **zero references to the router**. Every
number in docs 14–16 was real and none of it was reachable from the app.

## What was added

`app/route_tab.py` (~470 lines), rendered as the **first** tab, plus four
small edits to `streamlit_app.py`: the page config, a phone stylesheet, the
import, and the tab list. The old four tabs are untouched.

It talks only to `service.py`. It never sees a DataFrame, never builds a
graph, never learns what a morton code is.

## Mobile first, because that is where it runs

The demo is served from this Mac and watched **on a phone over Tailscale**, so
the usual Streamlit habits are all wrong:

| habit | why it fails on a phone | what we did |
|---|---|---|
| controls in the sidebar | the sidebar is a hidden hamburger drawer | the Thrill Dial is in the tab body |
| `st.selectbox` of presets | a native picker wheel, two taps, no context | full-width buttons that state *why* that pair |
| `layout="wide"` | nothing to widen into; also breaks the zoom fit | `layout="centered"` — and `view_for` already assumed a 700 px canvas |
| map tiles | with the network unplugged a tile map is a black rectangle | 17,345 OSM ways drawn as grey paths, `map_provider=None` |
| a slider to explore | 20–37 ms is fast, but on 200 O-D pairs the median demand gain is −0.00° | **Cruise and Send it on one map at once** |
| fixed `height=480` px | eats a whole phone screen | 430 px, overridden to `50vh` under a 640 px media query |

## What is on the screen

**Use case A.** Both dial settings drawn on the same map — Cruise in steel
blue, Send it in gold — under `compare()`'s own headline:

> Same two points. 1.13x the distance, 83% of it on different roads,
> +2.7 deg more lean asked of you.

Then one dial in detail: the line coloured segment-by-segment by fit (dim blue
= dull for you, gold = in your flow band), red pins where the gate **refused**
a road, the summary row, and `explain()`'s sentences printed verbatim.

**Use case B.** Four start presets × {1, 1.5, 2, 3} h, one map, and the loop's
own honest label when no tour fits the budget to within 20%.

## The three traps, handled rather than hidden

1. **`fun_score` compares routes at the same dial only.** Send it legitimately
   scores below Cruise. The tab prints the dial under the metric, puts the
   whole reason in the tooltip, and shows **mean lean asked** — which is
   absolute — right beside it.
2. **Outside the box there is no answer.** The free-entry boxes are clamped to
   47.38–48.03 N, 10.72–11.96 E, and the service's refusal sentence is shown
   as an error rather than an empty map: *"We have no crowd there, so we have
   no opinion."*
3. **The dial does nothing on most pairs.** When `overlap > 0.60` and the
   demand gain is under 0.5°, the caption says so in plain words and points at
   the preset where it does work. An app that admits this is more convincing
   than one that pretends.

## A correction to doc 16

Doc 16 says *"switching rider does not change the route"*. That was measured
on the wrong pair. On **Kochel → Tegernsee** the gate genuinely bites and the
line moves a long way:

```
cell overlap between userA and bike_4e1a9d64, same points
  Cruise   z* 0.15    0.730
  Send it  z* 0.90    0.105      <- 90% different road for a different rider
refusals on that pair: userA 3, bike_da67fa06 5, bike_4e1a9d64 4
```

So the rider switch **is** demonstrable on the map — just not on the pair doc
16 tested. That preset is now labelled as the safety-and-rider demo, and the
dial demo stays on Lenggries → Bad Tölz. The doc-16 warning still holds for
the other two pairs.

## Verified by running it, not by reading it

`streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest` executes the real script and surfaces any
exception:

```
5 tabs render, 0 exceptions
27 combinations swept: 3 riders x 3 preset pairs x 3 dial settings, all clean
16 loop combinations: 4 starts x 4 durations, all render
refusal pins fire on Kochel -> Tegernsee with their reason strings
out-of-coverage start returns the refusal sentence, not a blank map
```

Then served for real and fetched from the Linux box over the tailnet:
`200 in 0.048 s`.

## A security bug the launch command introduced

`--server.address=0.0.0.0` binds **every** interface. On this network the Mac
also holds a routable public address, and Streamlit printed it:

```
External URL: http://141.70.42.255:8501
```

That is an app backed by NDA data, published to the open internet. Fixed by
`run_demo.sh`, which binds the tailnet address only:

```
TCP 100.80.210.100:8501 (LISTEN)      <- and nothing else
tailnet  200      public IP  000 (refused)
```

`--lan` and `--local` exist for fallbacks. **Never `tailscale funnel` or
`tailscale serve --funnel`** — same NDA reason, larger blast radius.

## Running it

```bash
ssh macmini
cd ~/ehl_urich/flowstate
./run_demo.sh                 # http://100.80.210.100:8501 on the phone
./run_demo.sh --lan           # conference Wi-Fi usually isolates clients;
                              # prefer the phone's hotspot with the Mac joined
```

Rebake first if the router, the cell table or the OSM layer changed:
`/Users/mulaydm10/ehl_urich/.venv/bin/python analysis/14_bake_demo.py`.

**Phase 3 is done, pushed as `6d8fd68`, and both machines are clean.** The app is live right now at `http://100.80.210.100:8501` — open it on the phone.

## What's on screen

`app/route_tab.py` (~470 lines) is the first tab and talks only to `service.py`. Two use cases:

- **A → B** — Cruise and Send it drawn on *one* map at once (steel blue / gold) under `compare()`'s own headline, then one dial in detail: the line coloured segment-by-segment by fit, red pins where the gate refused a road, `explain()`'s sentences printed verbatim.
- **Loop for X hours** — 4 starts × {1, 1.5, 2, 3} h, with the loop's honest label when nothing fits the budget.

Mobile-first throughout: dial in the tab body, full-width preset buttons that state *why* that pair, `layout="centered"`, 17,345 cached OSM ways instead of tiles, map height overridden to `50vh` under 640 px.

## Verified by running it

`streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest` executes the real script, so exceptions surface:

```
5 tabs, 0 exceptions
27 rider × preset × dial combinations — all clean
16 loop combinations — all render
refusal pins carry their reason strings
out-of-coverage start → the refusal sentence, not a blank map
served over Tailscale, fetched from this box: 200 in 0.048 s
```

## Two things I found

**Doc 16 was wrong about the rider switch** — measured on the wrong pair. On Kochel → Tegernsee the gate genuinely bites: `userA` vs `bike_4e1a9d64` share 73% of cells at Cruise and **10% at Send it**, with 3–5 roads refused outright. So the rider switch *is* demonstrable on the map. Doc 16 corrected, that preset relabelled as the safety/rider demo, dial demo stays on Lenggries → Bad Tölz.

**The launch command you gave me publishes the demo to the internet.** `--server.address=0.0.0.0` binds every interface, and this Mac holds a routable public address on the conference network — Streamlit printed `External URL: http://141.70.42.255:8501`. Docs 13–17 are the record; verdicts at 41 rows (F94–F96).

It's ~01:00; freeze at 08:00. I read `06_PITCH.md` to be concrete — **it's worse than "slide 2 is dead."** Five of the five rehearsed demo beats describe things that are disproved or don't exist:

| Pitch says | Reality |
|---|---|
| Slide 2: "seven degrees stronger on left-handers" | asymmetry **tested and rejected** |
| Beat 1: "Cruise 40 min → Flow 58 min", drag the dial | detour ceiling is **1.137×**; we deliberately show both at once |
| Beat 1: "for a different rider this option is greyed out" | not a feature |
| Beat 2: "2.4 sets of lights/km, 61% built-up" | those numbers don't exist |
| Beat 3: "counter-clockwise, 31% more of the corners they're good at" | rests on the **disproved** asymmetry; loop direction isn't a feature |
| Beat 4: time-aware weather | **dropped**; cold-grip didn't replicate |
| Slide 6: "measured contribution from the ablation" | no ablation was ever run |
| Slide 7: "leave-one-rider-out" | there is **one** rider in the data — LORO is impossible |

If anyone reads that deck on stage, the demo contradicts the slides live. That is the single largest risk left, and it's much larger than anything in the app.

## Next steps, in order

**1 · Phase 5 — rewrite the pitch (~2 h, 01:00–03:00).** A rewrite, not an edit. The good news is the replacement material is stronger than what it replaces and is all measured:

- the gate lands within 3% of the hardest road this rider ever chose, independently at two cell sizes — the best number the project produced
- 52% of cells where OSM knows a limit have crowd p85 above it; re-pricing at the posted limit drops demand 9.67° → 5.60°. "We never recommend speeding" as a term in the cost function
- the honest headline: same two points, ~same distance, **83% different roads, +38% demand**
- Kochel → Tegernsee: change rider, and 90% of the road changes, with 3–5 roads refused outright
- one curve produces both Fun Score and Rider Safety
- what we disproved *about our own idea* and said so anyway — asymmetry, cold grip, the "three trip ids" card

**2 · Rewrite `10_LIVE_DEMO.md` to match the app that now exists (~30 min).** The demo script must be beats you can actually perform on the phone.

**3 · Phase 6 — rehearse on the phone, with the Mac's Wi-Fi off (~1 h, before 06:00).** Confirm the tailnet link on the phone's own hotspot, time the beats, check the gold/blue lines read at arm's length on a small screen.

**4 · Slack (03:00–08:00).** Free-click UX, anything the rehearsal exposes.

One decision that's yours: the deck itself. I can produce the rewritten pitch as markdown in the repo, or as a slide-shaped artifact you can present from. Say which and I'll start on Phase 5 now.

Ready. Current state is stable and pushed at `6d8fd68`, app live on the tailnet, both machines clean — so anything new lands on a working baseline rather than on top of unfinished work.

**Where new features plug in** — so you can tell me what you want in plain terms and I'll know the cost:

| Layer | File | What belongs here |
|---|---|---|
| physics / scoring | `router.py` → `score_cells` | anything that changes what a *cell* is worth (new flags, new penalties, new data columns) |
| topology / cost | `router.py` → `build_graph`, `_penalise` | anything that changes which *path* wins |
| new answer type | `router.py` → alongside `route_a_to_b` / `route_loop` | a third use case (waypoints, multi-day, "surprise me") |
| external data | `analysis/13_osm_layer.py` pattern | a new source, cached to `data/`, joined by cKDTree |
| exposure | `service.py` | every new thing needs a function here — the UI never reaches past it |
| pixels | `route_tab.py` | last, and cheap once the service function exists |

**Cheap** (minutes): new scoring terms, new penalties, new presets, new explain sentences, anything that reads columns already in the cell table.
**Medium** (an hour-ish): a new external layer following the OSM script's shape; a new routing objective.
**Expensive / risky**: anything needing `osmnx`, `geopandas`, `shapely`, `networkx` or `rasterio` — not installed, and the GDAL chain is a real risk to the environment. If a feature seems to need them, tell me and I'll find the NumPy/scipy route instead. `scipy.spatial.cKDTree` has covered every spatial join so far.

**Two standing rules for anything we add:**
- rebake after any change to the router, cell table or OSM layer — `analysis/14_bake_demo.py`, 2.4 s. The demo reads `demo.pkl`, not the repo.
- new data stays local and gitignored; nothing derived from the lake gets committed.

Tell me the features and I'll size them before writing anything. In the meantime, say the word if you want me to start the pitch rewrite in parallel — it's independent of the backend work and it's still the biggest open risk.

content.text:
Checked rather than guessed, and the answer is no — for two measured reasons, plus one that makes it unnecessary.

**Leaflet isn't a substitute for those three.** It's a different layer of the stack: osmnx fixes the *road network* (the 1.137× corridor ceiling), rasterio adds *gradient*, shapely fixes *line geometry*. Leaflet draws pixels. Swapping renderers changes nothing about what the router knows.

**Blocker 1 — it breaks the offline demo.** folium emits the Leaflet library itself from a CDN. I rendered a minimal map and counted the external requests:

```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/leaflet@1.9.3/dist/leaflet.js
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/leaflet@1.9.3/dist/leaflet.css
…10 external URLs in total
```

With the network unplugged — which is the hard requirement for the frozen demo — that map is **blank**, not degraded. Fixable by vendoring leaflet.js locally and repointing folium's `default_js`, but that's real work to get back to where we already are.

**Blocker 2 — the basemap is too big for it.** We draw 17,345 OSM ways / 76,116 points under every route. deck.gl pushes that to the GPU as WebGL. Leaflet draws SVG or canvas on the CPU. On a phone that's the difference between smooth panning and a slideshow.

**And the one thing Leaflet would genuinely buy, we can already do.** The real Leaflet advantage is tap-the-map-to-pick-points, which beats the number inputs we have now. Streamlit 1.63's `st.pydeck_chart` already supports it:

```
params: [pydeck_obj, width, use_container_width, height, selection_mode, on_select, key]
on_select: "ignore" | "rerun" | callable
```

So `on_select="rerun"` with a selectable cell layer gives tap-to-pick — offline, on the GPU, with no new dependency. Since routing snaps to cells anyway, tapping a cell *is* picking a point.

One caveat worth stating: tap-to-pick invites a judge to click two random points, and on a random pair the dial does almost nothing (median demand gain −0.00°). It's great for proving "this works anywhere in the box", bad as the moment you demo the dial. I'd add it as a secondary path, not the main one.

If the motivation was something else — the map looking plain, or wanting real satellite/terrain tiles behind the route — tell me which and I'll fix that directly in pydeck; tiles are a one-line change when there *is* network, and we already fall back cleanly when there isn't.
